about: Audio-only pronunciation dictionary for FAB / ONE narration. Applied to each cue's text before G2P; captions are never changed. Keys are whole words or phrases (matched on word boundaries, longest key first; spaces in a key match any run of whitespace). A key containing an uppercase letter matches case-sensitively, otherwise case-insensitively (override with "caseSensitive"). An alphabetic key also matches its inflections -s, -es, -'s, -s', -ed, -ing; phoneme entries then get misaki's suffix rules (e.g. resist -> resists, die -> dies). Each entry has exactly one of: "say" = a respelling substituted into the audio text and then read normally, or "phonemes" = Kokoro v1.0 / misaki British phonemes used verbatim (a string, or an object keyed by NOUN / VERB / ADJ / DEFAULT for noun-verb pairs). Symbols: A=eɪ I=aɪ Q=əʊ W=aʊ Y=ɔɪ ʤ ʧ, ᵊ = light schwa, a = TRAP, ɑː = PALM, ɒ = LOT, ɔː = THOUGHT, ɜː = NURSE, ː = long, ˈ primary and ˌ secondary stress (placed just before the stressed vowel). Optional "asr" lists transcriptions the automatic ASR check should accept for this entry (QA only; it never changes the audio). Where the audio should say different WORDS from the caption (e.g. 'deep ultraviolet' for 'DUV'), write those words in the script instead, so captions and speech match.

FAB / ONE.note: the app's name; the slash is not read

nm.note: unit after a number ('193 nm'); plural even for 1 nm, so prefer writing the word

resist.note: noun and verb both ri-ZIST; also matches resists / resist's

polysilicon.note: POL-ee-SIL-i-kun (not in misaki's lexicon; espeak would be the fallback)

implant.note: noun IM-plahnt (default: the usual reading in fab narration), verb im-PLAHNT after to/can/will or before a determiner

DUV.note: letters D U V, matching the caption. Write 'deep ultraviolet' in the script where those words should be heard.

EUV.note: letters E U V, matching the caption. Write 'extreme ultraviolet' in the script where those words should be heard.

TMAH.note: letters T M A H (British 'aitch'); the developer tetramethylammonium hydroxide

HMDS.note: letters H M D S (British 'aitch'); the adhesion primer

die.note: dye (one chip site on the wafer)

dies.note: dyes (plural used in the fab; not 'dice')

193.note: the ArF wavelength as lithographers say it ('one-ninety-three nanometre'); the caption keeps the digits

plasma.note: PLAZ-muh, with no linking r before a vowel ('plasma etch')

ultrapure.note: UL-truh-pure (espeak fallback gave a wrong first vowel)

implanted.note: im-PLAHN-tid (the adjective takes the verb's stress)
